# API reference

<!-- GENERATED by scripts/gen-reference.mjs from src/ — do not edit by hand.
     Regenerate: npm run docs:reference · Check: npm run docs:check -->

Every method below is on a client reachable from `const tfl5 = new TFL5(config)`.
`app_tid` is filled in from `tfl5.useApp(appTid)` unless you pass one.
Guides: [getting started](getting-started.md) · [authentication](authentication.md) ·
[data](data.md) · [files and sites](files-and-sites.md) · [realtime](realtime.md) ·
[billing](billing.md) · [errors](errors.md).

## TFL5 (root client)

| STT | Method | Endpoint | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `tfl5.useApp(appTid: string): this` | — | Scope subsequent calls to an app — `app_tid` is auto-injected. |
| 2 | `tfl5.get appId(): string \| undefined` | — | Currently scoped app tid, if any. |
| 3 | `tfl5.resource(ma: string): ResourceClient<T>` | — | A client bound to one resource by its machine alias. |
| 4 | `tfl5.createResource(input: NewResource): Promise<{ tid: string; ma: string }>` | — | Same as `tfl5.resources.create()` (kept for existing callers). |
| 5 | `tfl5.operator(opId: string): OperatorClient` | — | A client bound to one operator (catalog or tenant WASM). |
| 6 | `tfl5.setToken(token: string \| undefined): void` | — | Set/replace the Bearer token (service tokens, `auth: "bearer"`). |
| 7 | `tfl5.raw(path: string, body: Record<string, unknown> = {}): Promise<T>` | — | Escape hatch: POST a raw JSON body to any endpoint, get unwrapped `data`. Use when an endpoint isn't yet covered by a typed client. |

## tfl5.auth — AuthClient

| STT | Method | Endpoint | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `tfl5.auth.login(username: string, password: string): Promise<LoginResult>` | `/login` | Username/password login. Sets the session cookie (kept in the SDK's cookie jar outside a browser) and resolves `{ user: { tid, username } }`. |
| 2 | `tfl5.auth.register(input: Record<string, unknown>): Promise<unknown>` | `/reg` | Register a new user. |
| 3 | `tfl5.auth.logout(): Promise<void>` | `/logout` | Invalidate the current session (clears cookie / server session). |
| 4 | `tfl5.auth.me(): Promise<CurrentUser>` | `/user` | The signed-in user (`/user`). Throws `UnauthorizedError` when signed out. |
| 5 | `tfl5.auth.setToken(token: string \| undefined): void` | — | Manually set a Bearer token (e.g. one minted out-of-band). |
| 6 | `tfl5.auth.exportData(): Promise<DataExport>` | `/user/data/export` | Export the caller's own account: profile + email metadata + app memberships (right to access / data portability). Self-scoped — there is no admin-override form. Plaintext email addresses are fetched separately via `POST /user/email/list`; documents/files inside each app are exported through that app's own `/app/doc/*` and `/app/file/*` APIs. |
| 7 | `tfl5.auth.eraseAccount(confirm: { password?: string; code?: string } = {}): Promise<EraseResult>` | `/user/data/erase` | Request erasure of the caller's own account (right to be forgotten). On success stamps the request, signs the caller out on every device (treat yourself as logged out afterwards), and returns the schedule (`{ result, erase_after, ... }`); the hard erase runs in the background after a grace window (default 24h) during which {@link cancelErase} can withdraw it. |
| 8 | `tfl5.auth.cancelErase(): Promise<EraseResult>` | `/user/data/erase/cancel` | Withdraw a pending erasure request (only valid inside the grace window, on a fresh login). THROWS a {@link Tfl5Error } with `code:'no_pending_erasure'` if there is nothing to cancel. |
| 9 | `tfl5.auth.google(credential: string, opts: { password?: string } = {}): Promise<LoginResult>` | `/auth/google` | Google Identity Services sign-in. Pass the JWT string GIS hands your callback — `response.credential` (the field is literally named `credential`; it is *not* an OAuth `id_token` query param). On a fresh email or an already-verified account this establishes the session and resolves the {@link LoginResult}. |
| 10 | `tfl5.auth.microsoft(credential: string, opts: { password?: string } = {}): Promise<LoginResult>` | `/auth/microsoft` | Exchange a Microsoft (Azure AD) ID token for a tfl5 session. `credential` is the `idToken` from an MSAL.js `loginPopup`/`ssoSilent` result under the `common` authority. Same account-link semantics as {@link google}: if an existing account owns the email and can't be safely auto-linked, the call throws a `BadRequestError` whose `body.requires_password` is true — re-call with `{ password }` to link. |
| 11 | `tfl5.auth.magicLink(email: string, opts: { redirectTo?: string } = {}): Promise<unknown>` | `/auth/email-link` | Email a one-time sign-in link. Always answers success, whether or not the address has an account (so it cannot be used to probe addresses). `redirectTo` is where the browser lands after the link signs it in. |
| 12 | `tfl5.auth.phoneStart(phone: string, opts: { redirectTo?: string } = {}): Promise<unknown>` | `/auth/phone/start` | Start phone OTP (Zalo ZNS). Anti-enumeration: always success-shaped. |
| 13 | `tfl5.auth.phoneVerify(phone: string, code: string, opts: { redirectTo?: string } = {}): Promise<LoginResult>` | `/auth/phone/verify` | Complete phone OTP with the code the user received. |
| 14 | `tfl5.auth.qrStart(): Promise<QrStartResult>` | `/auth/qr/start` | Desktop side: open a QR session. |
| 15 | `tfl5.auth.qrPoll(sessionId: string): Promise<QrPollResult>` | `/auth/qr/poll` | Desktop side: poll the QR session. When the phone has approved, the first poll that sees it returns `status: "consumed"` with `user` and sets the session cookie on this client. |
| 16 | `tfl5.auth.qrApprove(sessionId: string): Promise<{ approved: true }>` | `/auth/qr/approve` | Phone side (must be signed in): approve the desktop sign-in. |
| 17 | `tfl5.auth.qrReject(sessionId: string): Promise<{ rejected: true }>` | `/auth/qr/reject` | Phone side (no sign-in needed): decline the desktop sign-in. |
| 18 | `tfl5.auth.telegramLogin(payload: TelegramWidgetPayload): Promise<{ username: string }>` | `/auth/telegram/login` | Sign in with a Telegram account that was linked earlier. |
| 19 | `tfl5.auth.telegramLink(payload: TelegramWidgetPayload): Promise<{ linked: true; telegram_id: number; telegram_username: string \| null }>` | `/auth/telegram/link` | Link a Telegram account to the signed-in user. |
| 20 | `tfl5.auth.telegramUnlink(): Promise<{ unlinked: boolean }>` | `/auth/telegram/unlink` | Remove the signed-in user's Telegram link. |
| 21 | `tfl5.auth.telegramStatus(): Promise<TelegramStatus>` | `/auth/telegram/status` | Whether Telegram sign-in is configured, and the caller's link if any. |
| 22 | `tfl5.auth.vneidStart(input: { appTid?: string; redirectTo?: string } = {}): Promise<VneidStartResult>` | `/auth/vneid/start` | Begin a VNeID sign-in for an app that has the VNeID operator enabled. Navigate the browser to `authorize_url`; VNeID redirects back to the server, which sets the session cookie and sends the browser on to `redirectTo` (a same-site path starting with `/` or `#`). Do not call the callback URL yourself. |

## tfl5.apps — AppsClient

| STT | Method | Endpoint | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `tfl5.apps.list(): Promise<AppConfig[]>` | `/app/list` | Apps the current user belongs to. |
| 2 | `tfl5.apps.get(appTid: string): Promise<AppConfig>` | `/app/get` | One app's settings, including its ACL arrays and the caller's `my_level`. |
| 3 | `tfl5.apps.create(data: { name?: string; description?: string; icon?: string }): Promise<AppConfig>` | `/app/update` | Create a new app (omit `tid`). Only name/description/icon are honored in `data` — ACL fields here are REJECTED (use `setAcl`). |
| 4 | `tfl5.apps.update(tid: string, data: { name?: string; description?: string; icon?: string; single_page?: string; error_page?: string }): Promise<AppConfig>` | `/app/update` | Edit an app (Manager). `single_page` / `error_page` name a path served for unknown URLs / on 404; pass `""` to clear. ACL changes go through `setAcl`. |
| 5 | `tfl5.apps.del(appTid: string): Promise<void>` | `/app/del` | Delete an app (Owner). The first call soft-deletes it; calling again on a soft-deleted app destroys it and all its data for good. |
| 6 | `tfl5.apps.transferOwnership(appTid: string, newOwnerTid: string, opts: { keepOldAsManager?: boolean; reason?: string } = {}): Promise<void>` | `/app/transfer-ownership` | Hand the app to another user (Owner only). By default the previous owner loses access; pass `keepOldAsManager: true` to keep them as a Manager. |
| 7 | `tfl5.apps.setAcl(appTid: string, acl: AppAcl): Promise<void>` | `/app/acl-set` | Replace some of the app's ACL arrays (Manager). Each array you pass replaces the stored one; arrays you omit are kept. Role ids may be sent raw (`r-…`); the server stores them as `[r-…]`. |
| 8 | `tfl5.apps.members(opts: { search?: string; roleFilter?: string; limit?: number; offset?: number } = {}): Promise<{ members: AppMember[]; total: number; nextOffset: number \| null }>` | `/app/member/list` | One page of the app's members (Designer). Filter with `search` (username) or `roleFilter` (a role tid, or `"__direct"` for members granted directly). Pass the returned `nextOffset` as `offset` for the next page. |
| 9 | `tfl5.apps.invite(input: { email: string; roleTids?: string[]; redirectTo?: string; note?: string }): Promise<{ tid?: string; status: "sent" \| "user_already_exists" \| "would_send" \| (string & {}); user_tid?: string; }>` | `/app/invite-user` | Invite someone by email, optionally with roles. A new address gets a sign-in link (`status: "sent"`); an address that already has an account answers `status: "user_already_exists"` with its `user_tid` — add that user with `setMemberRoles()`. |
| 10 | `tfl5.apps.setMemberRoles(userTid: string, roleTids: string[]): Promise<void>` | `/app/member/set-roles` | Set a member's roles to exactly `roleTids` (Manager). |
| 11 | `tfl5.apps.removeMember(userTid: string): Promise<void>` | `/app/member/remove` | Remove a user from every role and direct grant in the app (Designer). |
| 12 | `tfl5.apps.searchMembers(query: string, opts: { limit?: number } = {}): Promise<Array<{ user_tid: string; username: string; display_name: string \| null }>>` | `/app/member/search` | Find users by username to add to the app (Designer). Case-insensitive substring match on `username` only; banned accounts are excluded. `query` must be at least 2 characters (else code `query_too_short`); `limit` defaults to 10, max 25. |

## tfl5.wasm — WasmClient

| STT | Method | Endpoint | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `tfl5.wasm.list(): Promise<unknown>` | `/app/wasm/list` | List uploaded versions + their active/public/min_license state. |
| 2 | `tfl5.wasm.upload(input: { op_id: string; version: string; bytecode: Uint8Array \| Blob; public?: boolean; min_license?: string; notes?: string; }): Promise<unknown>` | `/app/wasm/upload` | Upload a compiled `.wasm` module version. Stored **inactive** until `activate`. `version` is a caller-chosen label (alphanumeric + `. _ -`, ≤48 chars), immutable per `(op_id, version)`. `public: true` opts the operator into un-authed dispatch (webhooks/callbacks) with NO data bridge; default is Reader-gated with a per-user-scoped data bridge. At most 2 MiB per upload today (the request size limit applies before the server's own 10 MiB check). The server validates that the module loads and exports the ABI before storing it (`wasm_module_invalid`). |
| 3 | `tfl5.wasm.activate(opId: string, version: string): Promise<unknown>` | `/app/wasm/activate` | Activate a previously-uploaded version (`version` = the upload label). |

## tfl5.files — FilesClient

| STT | Method | Endpoint | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `tfl5.files.upload(parts: UploadPart \| UploadPart[], opts: UploadOptions = {}): Promise<UploadResult>` | `/app/file/upload` | Upload one or more files in a single multipart request (Editor). Max 50 MiB per file and 100 MiB per request; allowed extensions: html/css/js/json, images, fonts, text, sqlite/db/bin, wasm, zip/tar/gz. |
| 2 | `tfl5.files.list(opts: { stage?: FileStage; prefix?: string } = {}): Promise<FileEntry[]>` | `/app/file/list` | List the app's files in one stage (Reader; rows you cannot see are filtered out). Pass `prefix` to keep only paths under it — filtering is client-side, the server always returns the whole stage. |
| 3 | `tfl5.files.save(input: SaveInput): Promise<WrittenFile & { warnings?: FileWriteWarning[] }>` | `/app/file/save` | Write one file from base64 (Editor). Same limits as `upload()`. |
| 4 | `tfl5.files.get(path: string, opts: { stage?: FileStage } = {}): Promise<FileContent>` | `/app/file/get` | Read one file's content as base64 (Reader + the row's own ACL). Files over 10 MiB are refused with code `file_too_large` — use `signUrl()` for those. |
| 5 | `tfl5.files.signUrl(path: string, opts: { expires_in_sec?: number; stage?: FileStage } = {}): Promise<{ signed_url: string; expires_at: number; cache_seconds: number }>` | `/app/file/sign-url` | Mint a short-lived signed URL for a file. Returns a relative `signed_url` (`/_signed/<token>`) plus its expiry. Default TTL is 5 minutes (server cap: 1 hour), so mint at view time rather than persisting the URL. Aggregate-binding callers are rejected (`pii_aggregate_only`). |
| 6 | `tfl5.files.rename(path: string, newPath: string, opts: { stage?: FileStage } = {}): Promise<FileRenameResult>` | `/app/file/rename` | Move/rename a file or folder (Editor). |
| 7 | `tfl5.files.del(path: string, opts: { stage?: FileStage; recursive?: boolean } = {}): Promise<FileDeleteResult>` | `/app/file/del` | Soft-delete a file (moves it to the trash; see `trashList` / `restore`). Folders need `recursive: true`. |
| 8 | `tfl5.files.trashList(stage?: FileStage): Promise<TrashEntry[]>` | `/app/file/trash-list` | List trashed rows (Editor). Omit `stage` to list both stages. |
| 9 | `tfl5.files.restore(fileTid: string, opts: { newPath?: string } = {}): Promise<{ tid: string; path: string; original_path: string; renamed: boolean; stage: FileStage; is_dir: boolean }>` | `/app/file/restore` | Restore a trashed row by its `tid` (from `trashList`). Pass `newPath` when the original path has since been reused (files only). |
| 10 | `tfl5.files.purge(fileTid: string): Promise<{ tid: string; purged_size: number; is_dir: boolean }>` | `/app/file/purge` | Permanently delete a trashed row and its bytes (Manager). Irreversible — there is no confirmation step on the server. |
| 11 | `tfl5.files.aclSet(input: FileAclInput): Promise<FileAcl>` | `/app/file/acl-set` | Replace a file's row-level ACL (Manager). Returns the stored arrays. |
| 12 | `tfl5.files.createFolder(path: string, opts: { stage?: FileStage } = {}): Promise<{ tid: string; path: string; stage: FileStage; parent_tid: string \| null; is_dir: true }>` | `/app/folder/create` | Create a folder (Editor). Defaults to the release stage. |

|---|---|---|---|

## tfl5.bundle — BundleClient

| STT | Method | Endpoint | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `tfl5.bundle.upload(input: \| FormData \| { version: string; notes?: string; file: Blob \| File }): Promise<BundleUploadResult>` | `/app/bundle/upload` | Upload a zip archive as a new immutable bundle version. |
| 2 | `tfl5.bundle.activate(version: string): Promise<BundleActivateResult>` | `/app/bundle/activate` | Atomically flip `apps.current_bundle_version` to `version`. The previous active version is stashed for one-click rollback. |
| 3 | `tfl5.bundle.rollback(): Promise<BundleRollbackResult>` | `/app/bundle/rollback` | Swap `current_bundle_version` ↔ `previous_bundle_version`. Fails if there is no previous version recorded. |
| 4 | `tfl5.bundle.unpublish(): Promise<BundleUnpublishResult>` | `/app/bundle/unpublish` | Take the site offline by NULLing `current_bundle_version`. The cleared version is stashed as `previous`, so `rollback()` or a fresh `activate()` re-publishes it. |
| 5 | `tfl5.bundle.list(limit?: number): Promise<BundleListResult>` | `/app/bundle/list` | List bundle versions for the app, newest first. |
| 6 | `tfl5.bundle.delete(version: string): Promise<BundleDeleteResult>` | `/app/bundle/delete` | Delete a stored bundle version and its files (Manager). Refused with `bundle_is_live` for the active version and `bundle_is_rollback_target` for the previous one; `bundle_not_found` when it does not exist. |

## tfl5.stages — StagesClient

| STT | Method | Endpoint | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `tfl5.stages.promote(dryRun = false): Promise<ReleaseResult>` | `/app/release` | Promote test-stage files to release (Manager). The promote runs in the background: the call returns `{ queued: true, job_id }` — poll `releaseStatus(job_id)`. The current release is backed up first. Resolves `result: false` (not an error) when the test stage is empty. |
| 2 | `tfl5.stages.releaseStatus(jobId: string): Promise<ReleaseStatus>` | `/app/release/status` | Progress of a queued promote (Manager of the job's app). |
| 3 | `tfl5.stages.listBackups(): Promise<ReleaseBackup[]>` | `/app/release/list` | List available release backup snapshots, sorted newest first. Each entry carries `ts` (millisecond timestamp) and `has_manifest`. |
| 4 | `tfl5.stages.rollbackRelease(backupTs?: number): Promise<ReleaseRollbackResult>` | `/app/release/rollback` | Roll the release stage back (Manager). With `backupTs` (from `listBackups()`) the release is restored from that snapshot, after a safety backup of the current one. Without it, the previous release becomes current again (an instant pointer swap). Resolves `result: false` (not an error) when a release is running or the backup does not exist. |
| 5 | `tfl5.stages.testStatus(): Promise<TestStageStatus>` | `/app/test/status` | Read test-stage quota and TTL metadata. Readable by any app Reader. |
| 6 | `tfl5.stages.testWipe(): Promise<TestWipeResult>` | `/app/test/wipe` | Immediately destroy all test-stage files (rows + bytes). Requires Manager permission. |

## tfl5.email — EmailClient

| STT | Method | Endpoint | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `tfl5.email.send(input: SendEmailInput): Promise<SendEmailResult>` | `/app/email/send` | Send a transactional email from the app's DKIM-configured domain. Returns queued metadata (async default) or delivery confirmation (sync when `TFL5_QUEUE_SYNC=1`). Requires Manager on the app. |
| 2 | `tfl5.email.listSends(input: ListSendsInput = {}): Promise<EmailSendRecord[]>` | `/app/email/sends` | List the outbound send audit log. Requires Reader on the app. |
| 3 | `tfl5.email.inbox(input: ListInboxInput = {}): Promise<InboxMessage[]>` | `/app/email/inbox` | List the per-app catch-all inbox. Requires Reader on the app. |
| 4 | `tfl5.email.markRead(input: MarkReadInput = {}): Promise<MarkReadResult>` | `/app/email/mark-read` | Mark inbox messages as read. Pass `email_tid` to target one message, or omit to mark all unread messages as read. Requires Editor on the app. |
| 5 | `tfl5.email.dkimCreate(input: DkimCreateInput): Promise<DkimCreateResult>` | `/app/email/dkim/create` | Mint a new DKIM keypair for the given domain and persist it to the app. The public DNS value must be published as a TXT record before sending. Upserts on `(app_tid, domain, selector)`. Requires Manager on the app. |
| 6 | `tfl5.email.dkimList(): Promise<DkimRecord[]>` | `/app/email/dkim/list` | List the DKIM keys registered for the app. Returns selector, domain, and the public DNS value for each key. Requires Reader on the app. |
| 7 | `tfl5.email.dnsRecords(input: DnsRecordsInput): Promise<DnsRecordsResult>` | `/app/email/dns-records` | Assemble the full set of SPF, DKIM, DMARC, and MX DNS records needed for the given domain. A DKIM key for the domain must exist (create via `dkimCreate` first). Requires Reader on the app. |

## tfl5.account — AccountClient

| STT | Method | Endpoint | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `tfl5.account.profile(): Promise<Profile>` | `/user/profile` | Fetch the extended profile for the authenticated user: decrypted email, name, mobile, license tier, all email addresses, auth methods, storage, and app count. |
| 2 | `tfl5.account.updateProfile(input: ProfileUpdateInput): Promise<void>` | `/user/profile/update` | Update the authenticated user's display name and/or mobile number. Pass `name: ""` or `mobile: ""` to clear the field; omit to leave unchanged. |
| 3 | `tfl5.account.changePassword(input: ChangePasswordInput): Promise<void>` | `/user/change-password` | Change the authenticated user's password. Requires the current password. Logs out all other sessions; the calling session gets a refreshed cookie. Throws for Google-only accounts (no `'password'` in `auth_methods`). |
| 4 | `tfl5.account.setPassword(input: { new: string; re_new?: string; code?: string }): Promise<{ result: boolean; msg?: string; }>` | `/user/set-password` | Give a PASSWORDLESS account (magic-link / OAuth / phone) its first password so it isn't locked to one sign-in method. No old password is required — the active session is the proof — but if the account has a confirmed 2FA enrolment the response is `{ code: "totp_required" }` until you re-call with `{ code }` (a TOTP or backup code). Accounts that already have a password are rejected (`code: "has_password"`); use {@link changePassword} instead. |
| 5 | `tfl5.account.changeUsername(newUsername: string): Promise<{ result: boolean; username?: string; msg?: string }>` | `/user/username/change` | Rename the account's login username. ACL membership is keyed on the stable user id, so permissions are preserved; legacy app-ownership rows are migrated server-side. Other sessions are signed out (their cookies carried the old name); this session's cookie is re-minted. |
| 6 | `tfl5.account.linkProvider(provider: "google" \| "microsoft", credential: string): Promise<{ result: boolean; msg?: string; auth_methods?: string[]; }>` | `/user/link` | Connect a Google/Microsoft identity to the CURRENT signed-in account. `credential` is the provider's ID token (GIS credential / MSAL idToken). Linking is email-based: the provider's email must match one of your account's emails, else the response carries `code: "email_mismatch"`. |
| 7 | `tfl5.account.sendVerification(): Promise<void>` | `/user/send-verification` | Trigger a verification email to the authenticated user's primary email address. Requires Mailler + `TFL5_NOREPLY_FROM` configured. No-op if already verified. |
| 8 | `tfl5.account.twoFaStatus(): Promise<TwoFaStatus>` | `/user/2fa/status` | Return the current 2FA enrolment state: `enrolled`, `confirmed`, `enrolled_at`, `last_used_at`, `backup_codes_remaining`. Never leaks the secret. |
| 9 | `tfl5.account.twoFaEnroll(): Promise<TwoFaEnrollResult>` | `/user/2fa/enroll` | Start TOTP enrolment. Generates a new secret + 8 backup codes, persists them encrypted, and returns the `otpauth://` provisioning URI (render as QR), the raw base32 secret (manual entry fallback), and the plaintext backup codes. |
| 10 | `tfl5.account.twoFaConfirm(code: string): Promise<TwoFaConfirmResult>` | `/user/2fa/confirm` | Confirm the TOTP enrolment by supplying the first valid 6-digit code from the authenticator app. Stamps `confirmed_at`; the 2FA gate now takes effect for this user. |
| 11 | `tfl5.account.twoFaVerify(code: string): Promise<TwoFaVerifyResult>` | `/user/2fa/verify` | In-session step-up challenge. Accepts a fresh 6-digit TOTP or a one-shot backup code. On success issues the `_2fa_verified` cookie (valid for `twofa_verify_ttl_ms`, default 30 min) that unlocks `/admin/*` when `TFL5_REQUIRE_2FA_FOR_ADMIN` is on. |
| 12 | `tfl5.account.twoFaDisable(code: string): Promise<TwoFaDisableResult>` | `/user/2fa/disable` | Disable 2FA. Requires proof-of-possession: a valid TOTP or backup code. Removes the enrolment row and clears the `_2fa_verified` cookie. |
| 13 | `tfl5.account.twoFaRegenerateBackupCodes(code: string): Promise<TwoFaRegenerateResult>` | `/user/2fa/regenerate-backup-codes` | Replace the backup codes. Requires proof-of-possession: a valid TOTP or existing backup code. All previous backup codes are invalidated immediately. |
| 14 | `tfl5.account.emailList(): Promise<UserEmail[]>` | `/user/email/list` | List all email addresses for the authenticated user (primary + secondaries), sorted primary-first then by `added_at`. Each entry includes `email_hash` (hex SHA-256) for use as the key in remove / promote / send-verification. |
| 15 | `tfl5.account.emailAdd(input: EmailAddInput): Promise<{ email_hash: string }>` | `/user/email/add` | Add a secondary email address. Automatically fires a verification email. The row stays unverified until the user clicks the link; promoting an unverified secondary to primary is refused. |
| 16 | `tfl5.account.emailRemove(input: EmailByHashInput): Promise<void>` | `/user/email/remove` | Remove a secondary email. Identified by hex `email_hash` (from `emailList()`). Refuses the primary address — promote another first. |
| 17 | `tfl5.account.emailPromotePrimary(input: EmailByHashInput): Promise<void>` | `/user/email/promote-primary` | Promote a verified secondary email to primary. The address must be verified first; promoting an unverified one is refused. Updates `users.email_*` so password reset, Google linking, and `/user/profile` all see the new primary address. |
| 18 | `tfl5.account.emailSendVerification(input: EmailByHashInput): Promise<void>` | `/user/email/send-verification` | Resend the verification link for any email address the caller owns (primary or secondary). Identified by hex `email_hash`. Refuses already-verified rows. |

| STT | Method | Endpoint | Description |

| 1 | `tfl5.domain.preview(domain: string): Promise<DomainPreviewResult>` | `/app/domain/preview` | Mint DNS instructions for a domain — no DB write. For public hosts, the domain's A record must already point at this server. For local-dev (`*.localhost`), subdomain shortcuts, and delegations the verification step is skipped automatically. |
| 3 | `tfl5.domain.list(): Promise<DomainRecord[]>` | `/app/domain/list` | List all custom domains bound to the app (Designer+ permission). |
| 4 | `tfl5.domain.del(tid: string): Promise<void>` | `/app/domain/del` | Remove a domain binding by its `tid`. Requires Owner permission. |
| 5 | `tfl5.domain.verify(tid: string): Promise<DomainAddResult>` | `/app/domain/verify` | Re-check DNS and re-activate an inactive domain row. Accepts both the new A-record method and the legacy TXT-token method. |
| 6 | `tfl5.domain.setMode(domain: string, mode: "private" \| "public"): Promise<{ domain: string; mode: string; auto_populated_default_rules: boolean }>` | `/app/domain/mode` | Toggle the delegation mode for a parent domain. `mode` must be `"private"` (default, explicit whitelist required) or `"public"` (any authenticated user may bind subs; label rules still apply). First flip to public auto-populates fail-safe default label rules. |
| 7 | `tfl5.domain.setLabelRules(domain: string, rules: { allow: string[]; deny: string[] }): Promise<{ domain: string; allow_count: number; deny_count: number }>` | `/app/domain/label-rules` | Replace the `allow` / `deny` regex label-rule sets for a parent domain. Patterns target the sub-prefix (everything before `.<parent>`). Max 10 patterns per list, max 200 chars each. Pass empty arrays to clear. |
| 8 | `tfl5.domain.getConfig(domain: string): Promise<DelegationConfig>` | `/app/domain/get-config` | Read the current delegation config (mode + label rules + whitelist count) for a parent domain. Owner only. |
| 9 | `tfl5.domain.testPattern(domain: string, label: string, rules: { allow: string[]; deny: string[] }): Promise<TestPatternResult>` | `/app/domain/delegation/test-pattern` | Dry-run a candidate `allow`/`deny` ruleset against a single label without persisting anything. Returns `verdict`, `matched_pattern`, and `reason`. |
| 10 | `tfl5.domain.whitelistAdd(domain: string, granteeUserTid: string, opts: { expires_at?: number \| null; max_subs?: number \| null } = {}): Promise<{ tid: string; parent_domain: string; grantee_user_tid: string; expires_at: number \| null; max_subs: number \| null; }>` | `/app/domain/whitelist/add` | Grant `grantee_user_tid` the right to bind subdomains under `domain`. Re-granting rotates `expires_at` + `max_subs` atomically (upsert). Pass `max_subs: null` to lift an existing per-grantee cap. |
| 11 | `tfl5.domain.whitelistRemove(domain: string, granteeUserTid: string): Promise<{ parent_domain: string; removed_tid: string \| null; existing_subs_kept: boolean }>` | `/app/domain/whitelist/remove` | Revoke a delegation grant for `grantee_user_tid` under `domain`. Existing subdomains bound by the grantee are NOT removed. |
| 12 | `tfl5.domain.whitelistList(domain: string): Promise<WhitelistEntry[]>` | `/app/domain/whitelist/list` | List all whitelist (delegation) grants for a parent domain. Owner only. |
| 13 | `tfl5.domain.delegationsReceived(): Promise<ReceivedDelegation[]>` | `/app/domain/delegations/received` | List all parents the *caller* can bind subdomains under — both explicit whitelist grants and public-mode parents. No `app_tid` needed. |
| 14 | `tfl5.domain.reclaimSub(adminAppTid: string, subDomain: string, reason?: string): Promise<{ sub_domain: string; parent_domain: string; reclaimed_from_app_tid: string; }>` | `/app/domain/reclaim-sub` | Force-unbind a subdomain from whatever app currently holds it. The caller must own the parent app whose active domain is the longest-suffix ancestor of `subDomain`. `adminAppTid` is the caller's own app (used for auth only). |
| 15 | `tfl5.domain.subsOfParent(domain: string): Promise<SubDomainEntry[]>` | `/app/domain/subs-of-parent` | List every active subdomain currently bound under `domain`. Shows the app name + owner for each sub so the owner knows what they would reclaim. Owner only. |
| 16 | `tfl5.domain.requestAccess(domain: string, note?: string): Promise<{ tid: string; parent_domain: string; requested_host: string; status: "pending"; already_pending: boolean; }>` | `/app/domain/request` | File a request to bind `domain` (a sub of a private parent). Only valid when `evaluate_delegation` returns `private_needs_request`. Idempotent — re-submitting a still-pending request returns the existing row with `already_pending: true`. |

| 9 | `tfl5.f3.grantsList(f3Tid: string): Promise<F3GrantRow[]>` | `/app/f3/grants/list` | List all grant rows for a file (Manager on the app). Includes revoked rows (check `revoked_at != null`). |

One socket carries either a single `key` or up to {@link SUBSCRIBE_KEYS_MAX} `keys` of the SAME resource (single-resource form), OR up to {@link SUBSCRIBE_KEYS_MAX} `{resource, key}` pairs across MULTIPLE resources (multi-resource form via `subs`). ## tfl5.resource(ma) — ResourceClient

| STT | Method | Endpoint | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `tfl5.resource(ma).create(data: T): Promise<{ tid: string; resource_tid: string }>` | `/app/doc/create` | Create one doc. Resolves its `tid` (use `get()` to read it back). |
| 2 | `tfl5.resource(ma).createBatch(items: Array<{ data: T } & DocAcl>, opts: { atomic?: boolean } = {}): Promise<{ tids: string[]; count: number; failures?: Array<{ index: number; code: string; msg: string; [k: string]: unknown }> }>` | `/app/doc/create-batch` | Create many docs in one round-trip. Each item is `{ data, ...acl }`. `atomic` (default true server-side) = all-or-nothing; pass false for partial-success import flows. Max 200 items/request. |
| 3 | `tfl5.resource(ma).get(tid: string): Promise<Doc<T>>` | `/app/doc/get` | Fetch one doc by tid (secret fields decrypted). |
| 4 | `tfl5.resource(ma).list(opts: ListOptions = {}): Promise<Doc<T>[]>` | `/app/doc/list` | List docs, optionally filtered/paged. `where` is a containment + comparison filter evaluated against `data_indexed` (level-0 fields only — secret fields are not searchable by design). |
| 5 | `tfl5.resource(ma).listPage(opts: ListOptions = {}): Promise<{ docs: Doc<T>[]; nextCursor?: string }>` | `/app/doc/list` | One page of `list()` plus the keyset cursor for the next page. Pass the returned `nextCursor` back as `cursor`; it is `undefined` on the last page. Prefer this over large `offset` values (the server caps offset). |
| 6 | `tfl5.resource(ma).importFile(input: { file: Blob; filename?: string; mapping?: Record<string, string>; atomic?: boolean; }): Promise<ImportResult>` | `/app/doc/import` | Bulk-import rows from a `.csv` or `.xlsx` file (Editor, max 20 MiB and 5000 rows). The first row is the header. With `mapping` (`{ "Header text": "field" }`) only mapped columns are imported; without it each header is used as the field name. Rows go through the same validation and hooks as `create()`. With `atomic: true` each chunk of 200 rows is all-or-nothing; otherwise failed rows are reported in `failures` (with their 1-based row number in the file) and the rest are kept. Use `tfl5.resources.previewImport(file)` to infer fields first. |
| 7 | `tfl5.resource(ma).update(tid: string, data: T): Promise<{ tid: string }>` | `/app/doc/update` | Update by tid. NOTE: `data` REPLACES the doc's data wholesale — any field not present is removed (the server re-splits the new object into data_indexed/data_secret). To change a few fields, `get()` first and send the merged object; for an ACL-only change use `setAcl()`. |
| 8 | `tfl5.resource(ma).patch(tid: string, partial: Partial<T>): Promise<{ tid: string }>` | — | Convenience partial update: get → shallow-merge → full-replace update. Not atomic (read-modify-write races a concurrent writer). |
| 9 | `tfl5.resource(ma).upsert(input: { match_on?: Record<string, unknown>; data: T; editors?: string[]; readers?: string[]; deletable?: string[]; noaccess?: string[]; }): Promise<{ tid: string; created: boolean; resource_tid: string }>` | `/app/doc/upsert` | Insert-or-update. `match_on` is a flat dict of LEVEL-0 fields used to find an existing row via JSONB containment — it MUST resolve to a unique row (the server rejects a match of >1). Secret fields cannot be matched on. Omit `match_on` (or match nothing) → insert. |
| 10 | `tfl5.resource(ma).del(tid: string): Promise<void>` | `/app/doc/del` | Soft-delete a doc. |
| 11 | `tfl5.resource(ma).setAcl(tid: string, acl: DocAcl): Promise<void>` | `/app/doc/acl-set` | Set per-doc ACL arrays (editors/readers/deletable/noaccess). |
| 12 | `tfl5.resource(ma).resolveTid(): Promise<string>` | `/app/resource/list` | Resolve this resource's tid from its ma (cached). |
| 13 | `tfl5.resource(ma).getSchema(): Promise<ResourceDef>` | `/app/resource/get` | Get this resource's definition (fields, hooks, ...). |
| 14 | `tfl5.resource(ma).putSchema(def: { name?: string; description?: string; /** Allow anonymous share links on this resource. */ sharing?: boolean; /** Resource ACL arrays; each one sent replaces the stored one. */ readers?: string[]; editors?: string[]; noaccess?: string[]; deletable?: string[]; fields?: FieldDecl[]; hooks?: Hook[]; before_create_code?: string; after_create_code?: string; before_update_code?: string; after_update_code?: string; }): Promise<{ tid: string }>` | `/app/resource/update` | Update this resource's definition (name/fields/hooks/code guards). To CREATE a new resource use `tfl5.resources.create(...)` instead. |
| 15 | `tfl5.resource(ma).setResourceAcl(acl: { readers?: string[]; editors?: string[]; noaccess?: string[]; deletable?: string[] }): Promise<void>` | — | Replace some of this resource's own ACL arrays (Manager). Arrays you omit are kept. Role ids may be sent raw (`r-…`); the server stores them bracketed. Who may read the resource's docs is decided here and at the app level — a doc's own arrays only govern writes. |
| 16 | `tfl5.resource(ma).destroy(): Promise<{ soft_deleted: true }>` | `/app/resource/del` | Delete this resource definition and its stored docs (Manager). The definition is soft-deleted; its doc storage is dropped. Refused with code `resource_referenced_by_link` while another resource's link field points at it. There is no confirmation step. |
| 17 | `tfl5.resource(ma).get hooks(): HooksAccessor` | — | Declarative-hook accessor (require_fields / set_fields / webhook / wasm). |
